short_description.en: Two separate series of images created using mixed media, linked by the use of collage and recycled materials.

description.en: Two separate series of images created using mixed media, linked by the use of collage and recycled materials. In the ‘ Materiaalin inspiraatio ’ series, the materials - old wall papers - have, quite literally, provided the inspiration for the subjects. The old wall papers were also the main the main materials used to create the works. The ideas for the subjects of the pictures arose from the colours, textures and patterns of the wallpapers. The colour palette evoked themes from Italy and Japanese culture, and the floral patterns gave rise to a floral arrangement. The ‘ Tuokiokuvia Toscanan matkalta ’ series was inspired by a trip to Tuscany. The subjects of the images are the experiences and feelings from the journey, as well as those before and after the trip. The aim is to invite the viewer on a journey into the light, colours and atmosphere of Tuscany. The works have been created using free publications such as shop customer magazines, as well as various other leaflets and used envelopes, from which very small pieces have been cut or torn and glued onto canvas. name.en: Hanna Rinne: Entities – Beings in Between (art exhibition)

short_description.en: In the works on display, playfulness and vibrancy go hand in hand with a subtle sense of melancholy and strangeness.

description.en:
Hanna Rinne (b. 1980) is a visual artist and graphic designer from Kirkkonummi. Her artistic practice lies at the intersection of pop surrealism and experimental contemporary art.

"I have always been fascinated by what happens when the cute and the strange collide. In my works, playfulness and colourfulness go hand in hand with subtle melancholy and strangeness.

The characters – or entities – that appear in my works represent forms of life that do not fit into traditional categories: they are not plants, animals, nor even entirely bacteria. They are something in between and all of these things at once. You may recognise something familiar in the figures, such as the shape of a berry, the surface of a mollusc or the structure of a cell, but you cannot name them with certainty.

The aim of my art is to spark curiosity and invite the viewer, for a moment, into a world where every being has its own story to tell."


The exhibition is open during the library’s opening hours. Welcome!

Curated by artist Rauha Hartt the exhibition titled "Ryteikkö" brings together three generations of artists who in their works in the exhibition explore the notion of the theme.

"Ryteikkö" means a thicket, copse or a tangly bit of the woods where accessibility is little or none. Thoroughly familiar for anyone who's ever walked in an even semi wild Finnish woods.

Ryteikkö can be seen as a physical place but also something like a mental block.

How'd you navigate this?

description.en:
Mauri Haapamäki, founder of Aspenhill Design Oy, represents the rare and rapidly disappearing silversmithing tradition in Finland.

Silversmithing, one of the related professions within the goldsmithing industry, involves the traditional handcrafted production of large silver objects using techniques such as spinning, hammering and raising.

With this year’s selection, the Finnish Goldsmiths’ Association wishes to highlight the demanding and significant craftsmanship of silversmithing, a profession that is increasingly under threat within the goldsmithing industry.

It is a craft that requires an exceptional level of skill and expertise – knowledge that can only be acquired through years of experience and practice.

description.en:
The retrospective exhibition of Howard Smith (1928–2021) presents the versatile career of a well-loved and distinctive artist.

The exhibition pays tribute to his open-minded visual expression and his influence on the Finnish art and design scene.

Originally from New Jersey, Smith became known for his curious approach to art. His extensive career resembled a continuous journey of exploration into the possibilities of different materials, forms and techniques.

Smith worked across a wide range of media, including ceramics, textile art, sculpture, papercut, collage and drawing.

In addition, his designs extended into urban spaces through numerous public artworks. Alongside his art, Smith designed fabrics for Vallila and ceramics for Arabia. His much-loved design classics have found their way into many Finnish homes and everyday life.

The long-awaited solo exhibition of Howard Smith is part of EMMA’s series highlighting both the classics of modernism and its reformers.

For the third time, EMMA presents the international group exhibition In Search of the Present, featuring leading contemporary artists whose works explore key phenomena and questions of modern times.

The 2026 exhibition, celebrating EMMA’s 20th anniversary, is an exploration of the now and an invitation to be present both in time and in place.

The exhibition features works by Marina Abramović, Haruka Kashima, Kimsooja, Tarik Kiswanson, Germaine Kruip, Ken Matsubara, Lydia Ourahmane, Helen Pashgian, Jani-Matti Salo, Danh Võ, WAUHAUS x TTK (Nurture), Ian Wilson, and Maaria Wirkkala.

short_description.en: Come and explore the museum’s collections in the long-awaited exhibition Traces of Craft.

description.en:
Come and explore the museum’s collections in the long-awaited exhibition Traces of Craft.

The collections of Museo Kruunu originated with the establishment of the Finnish School of Watchmaking in 1944 and the teaching collection it assembled through donations of various clocks, watches, and watchmaking tools.

In 2015, a project was launched to expand the museum concept to include not only horology and the watchmaking tradition, but also jewellery and goldsmithing. The collections also include an extensive archive, library, and photograph collection.

The exhibition Traces of Craft presents the museum’s collections in a broad scope, featuring both long-time favourites and more recent donations.

In the exhibition, you can explore not only the museum’s own history through its collections, but also Finnish watch and jewellery history through the objects used here and the stories they tell. These objects reflect Finnish cultural history, and the collections preserve the craftsmanship of numerous skilled artisans from the past.

description.en:
Draped – Art of Printed Fabrics exhibition will wrap EMMA’s exhibition galleries in vibrant colours and fascinating patterns of printed fabrics. The exhibition highlights printed fabrics by exceptional artists since the 1930s, and views them through the lens of art.

Printed fabrics are an integral part of Finnish design and everyday life; the patterns cover our homes, clothes our bodies and create memories. They touch us, communicate, convey meanings, and evoke memories. Through them, we have shaped identities and individuality, as well as a sense of security and belonging.

The exhibition opens in a space surrounded by the Bryk & Wirkkala visible storage, where changing exhibitions bring the life’s work of Rut Bryk and Tapio Wirkkala into dialogue with design classics and contemporary artists.

short_description.en: Kietoutumia (Intertwinings) unfolds throughout EMMA’s exhibition spaces as an interwoven encounter between two bodies and the visual arts.

description.en:
Kietoutumia (Intertwinings) unfolds throughout EMMA’s exhibition spaces as an interwoven encounter between two bodies and the visual arts. Combining contemporary vocal music and improvised contemporary dance, soprano Meeri Pulakka and dance artist Sofia Keto-Tokoi explore themes of intimacy, touch, memory, longing and finitude.

Making versatile use of the museum environment, the performance takes the form of a fragmented, moving experience in which visitors may immerse themselves in individual moments or follow the work as a whole.

The programme features solo vocal works by Enno Poppe, Jarkko Hartikainen and Rebecca Saunders, as well as Lunula, composed by Aino Tenkanen specifically for the duo.

Set to texts by Hara Hermunen and premiered at the Tampere Biennale, the work integrates dance as an inseparable part of the composition. Pulakka and Keto-Tokoi have been closely involved in the creative process, witnessing the emergence of both text and music.

short_description.en: The purpose is simply to sit together in silence for 45–60 minutes and honor life and the interconnected unity of all things.

description.en:
Welcome to an open, non-sectarian meditation group that brings meditation into the daily life of Espoo residents. We meet on Sunday mornings from 10 to 11 AM in whichever space the library designates at the time – usually in the group room Kajuutta or the larger stage area next to it.

The purpose is simply to sit together in silence for 45 minutes. This is not a therapy group, nor a discussion or teaching session. After the session there is time to catch up. We begin right after the library opens. The floor is carpeted wall-to-wall. The style is free. The library provides chairs and some cushions, and you are welcome to bring your own cushion as well. Meditation takes place as part of the library’s everyday life, so background sounds and occasional passers-by are part of the experience.

description.en:
Iina Paakki’s art exhibition at the Showcase Gallery on the upper floor of the Sello Library, 1–20 November 2026.

Iina Paakki is Helsinki-based artist with a passion for colour, who draws inspiration from things she perceives, in one way or another, as magical and mystical. She is fascinated by dreams, fairy tales, space and experiences that we cannot always explain through reason. In recent years, semi-abstract cloudscapes have played a central role in her art, a theme that continues in the ‘Paper Dreams’ exhibition at Sello Library. The Showcase Gallery features her colourful works, intuitively painted on canvas and paper, as well as a selection of prints.

More information: www.iinapaakki.fi

The exhibition is open during the library’s opening hours. Welcome!

name.en: Nanna Fri: "The journey of story and dream"

short_description.en: I capture a glimpse of the world of stories and dreams through images. Painting is a feeling that lives in the moment and cannot be controlled by force.

description.en:
“I read a story that I dreamed about last night. In the dream, there was a forested path along which I walked to a quiet town. The town's buildings were made of light and shadow, just like their inhabitants…”

I capture a glimpse of the world of stories and dreams through images. Painting is an emotion alive in the moment, which cannot be guided by force. From that moment, a trace remains, perhaps forgotten or longed for.

I hope that my paintings will create a dialogue between the viewer and the image, allowing for a moment of pause and the experience of the timeless dimension of being.

The creator of the paintings will be available on Sunday, November 1st, from 2 PM to 4 PM.

short_description.en: Moving in November: Giorgia Lolli – Body Sweats (for Elsa)

description.en:
Moving in November: Giorgia Lolli – Body Sweats (for Elsa)

Body Sweats (for Elsa) is an homage to Baroness Elsa von Freytag-Loringhoven (1874–1927), a poet and avant-garde artist, a pioneer of the Dada movement.

The title is taken from her eponymous collection of poems, an erotic and proto-punk manifesto. Created by choreographer Giorgia Lolli, the work combines dance, lecture performance, poetry reading, workout: sweat will be a way to explore the intertwining of effort and pleasure, the binding force of a heterogeneous collage of dance and textual materials.

Love letters between friends and lovers. Waterless aqua aerobics in tiger-striped leotards. A poem for the Baroness. A split, in her honour.

EMMA, Espoo

14.11. & 15.11.2026

15.00-16.00

Admission fee 10/20€

In English and Italian

Please note: loud music, proximity between audience and performers, liquorice candy (upon consent)

description.en:
Collection Kakkonen presenting Finnish glass and ceramic art, will be complemented by an exhibition dedicated to ceramic artist Gerda Thesleff (1871–1939).

Thesleff is one of the earliest artists represented in the collection and a pioneer of Finnish ceramic art. Her work will now be shown for the first time in a museum exhibition.

Gerda Thesleff studied at Helsinki’s Central School of Art and Design between 1898 and 1906, continuing her studies under the guidance of Alfred William Finch, renowned for his Iris ceramics. Thesleff developed a distinctive style that set her apart from her contemporaries.

She treated the surfaces of her hand-thrown vessels like canvases, painting freely with a brush to create a range of motifs. Her ceramics are adorned with imagery such as olive groves, cypress-covered hills, and landscapes overflowing with vines.

Many of these themes and colours were inspired by the travels and life that Gerda shared with her sister, visual artist Ellen Thesleff, in Tuscany, Italy.

Yksin vai yhdessä – Ensam eller tillsammans is a multidisciplinary work by dance artist Katriina Kantola and violinist Teija Kivinen. The piece combines contemporary dance, dance improvisation, contemporary violin music, traditional violin music, and Finland-Swedish poetry.

The work Yksin vai yhdessä – Ensam eller tillsammans tells the story of breaking free from loneliness toward interaction and connection with others. It encourages reflection on what it is like to be alone and isolated from others. The work also explores whether it is possible to feel connected to others even when physically distant from them. It encourages reaching out to others rather than withdrawing into oneself.

A young factory worker whom first the Reds and then the Whites try to recruit and force into their ranks. He stubbornly struggles to remain neutral.

A painter and wrestler from Tainionkoski. He seeks revenge for the way the bourgeoisie treated him and his brother.

And a young woman who leaves for Helsinki to work as a maid. She falls in love with a young man who ends up fighting in Joutseno. She follows him eastward and takes a position at a hospital ward in Lappeenranta. Concerned about her family, she crosses to the White side to visit her relatives.

short_description.en: The performance is a multidisciplinary work by dance artist Katriina Kantola and violinist Teija Kivinen.

description.en:
Yksin vai yhdessä – Ensam eller tillsammans

Monday, Dec. 7, at 6:00 p.m., Salonki, Lippulaiva Library

Yksin vai yhdessä – Ensam eller tillsammans is a multidisciplinary work by dance artist Katriina Kantola and violinist Teija Kivinen. The piece combines contemporary dance, dance improvisation, contemporary violin music, traditional violin music, and Finland-Swedish poetry.

The work Yksin vai yhdessä – Ensam eller tillsammans tells the story of breaking free from loneliness toward interaction and connection with others. It encourages reflection on what it is like to be alone and isolated from others. The work also explores whether it is possible to feel connected to others even when physically distant from them. It encourages reaching out to others rather than withdrawing into oneself.

short_description.en: Vuoksenniskan teloitetut is a historical novel that follows eight individuals who, through different paths, end up in the prison camp at Vuoksenniska.

description.en:

5 pm


Three men from the same village in Ruokolahti. They fight in the Red Guard in Joutseno. As the Reds retreat through Lappeenranta toward Vyborg, they travel against the tide.

Two men, a father and son, factory workers from Tainionkoski. They hide from the Whites and attempt to cross the ice of Lake Saimaa to reach the Red side in Lappeenranta.

A young factory worker whom first the Reds and then the Whites try to recruit and force into their ranks. He stubbornly struggles to remain neutral.

A painter and wrestler from Tainionkoski. He seeks revenge for the way the bourgeoisie treated him and his brother.

And a young woman who leaves for Helsinki to work as a maid. She falls in love with a young man who ends up fighting in Joutseno. She follows him eastward and takes a position at a hospital ward in Lappeenranta. Concerned about her family, she crosses to the White side to visit her relatives.

short_description.en: What happens when the anger simmering beneath the surface can no longer remain hidden? Mirva Karkinen talks about her bold and distinctive debut novel Leviatan.

description.en:
Author Mirva Karkinen will visit Iso Omena Library to discuss her debut novel Leviatan. The event will explore the origins of the work, its central themes, and the writing process. Karkinen will also read excerpts from the novel, and audience members will have the opportunity to join the discussion and ask questions.

Leviatan tells the story of women waiting for something to burst. Before a breaking point is reached, however, a person must be pushed to their limits, and so the women’s restrooms creak and groan.

Written with an aggressive and highly original voice, the novel examines the position of women in contemporary society, the invisible structures of power, and the misogyny that runs through the deeper currents of society. Leviatan is a story about inequality, but above all it is a plea for empathy.

Mirva Karkinen (born 1994) is a Helsinki-based Master of Arts in Literary Studies and Philosophy. Her interests include literature, power, and gender, and she has published feminist literary criticism as well as essays on the book industry.
